authorized_evidence.content:
Manager Responsibilities

Managers are responsible for setting clear expectations, maintaining team operating rhythm, supporting employee growth, approving time off, and escalating risks early. Managers should document important decisions and keep role expectations current.

Performance Documentation

Performance feedback should include specific examples, business impact, expected behavior, and follow-up actions. Managers should avoid vague labels and should distinguish between skill gaps, behavior concerns, and role mismatch.

Performance Improvement Process

When serious performance issues continue after feedback, managers should consult People Operations before starting a formal performance improvement process. Documentation should include expectations, timeline, support offered, and review checkpoints.

This guide does not contain salary bands or compensation formulas.

Escalation Paths

Employee relations concerns should be escalated to People Operations. Security access issues should be escalated to IT Support. Customer-impacting delivery risks should be escalated to the relevant department leader.

One-on-One Expectations

Managers should hold one-on-one meetings with direct reports at least every two weeks. Notes should focus on priorities, blockers, feedback, and growth needs. Sensitive personal details should not be recorded unless required for an HR process.

Conflict Handling

Managers should address team conflict early, document observed behavior, and avoid making unsupported conclusions about intent. Repeated conduct concerns should be discussed with People Operations.

Escalation Triggers

Escalate to a Manager when a customer reports suspected data exposure, repeated billing failures, executive escalation, blocked payroll or finance close, missed Enterprise SLA, or a production incident that affects more than one customer.

Escalate to Engineering through the incident channel when support can reproduce a product defect, a workaround is not available, or logs show repeated failures for the same customer workflow.

authorized_evidence.content:
Team Planning

Managers should maintain a quarterly team plan with goals, ownership, dependencies, and risks. Plans should identify customer-impacting work, hiring assumptions, and capacity constraints.

Employee Support Channels

General HR questions should be sent to People Operations. Benefits questions should be sent to the benefits support queue. Security access questions should be sent to IT Support. Performance or role expectation questions should first be discussed with the employee's manager.

Handoff Rules

When Sales receives a support issue, the Sales Representative should create or link the support case and include customer impact, account tier, urgency, and any promised follow-up. Sales should not run a parallel support process in private notes.

When Support identifies expansion, renewal risk, or contract dissatisfaction, Support should notify the account owner and Manager. The notification should distinguish product issue, adoption issue, billing issue, and contract issue.
